transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-15 14:00 UTC — Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Cruz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Nexa Procurement), Maya Singh (Nexa Legal), Liam O'Connor (Nexa CTO), Sara Kim (Nexa Security)

Summary: quick run-through of MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing tiers; focus on data residency and KMS integration. Agreed deliverables and timelines.

[00:00] Jamie Cruz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, is this still a good time?
[00:03] Tom Alvarez: yeah yep, good to go—thanks Jamie.
[00:06] Jamie Cruz: cool. quick intros, i'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. we'll run through the MSA/DPA points and the SLA/pricing stuff.
[00:18] Priya Nair: hi all, quick context — we've worked with healthcare customers on private deployments and hosted with strict dpa requirements, so we'll map options to your constraints.
[00:30] Maya Singh: thanks. our goal today is to get to a point where legal can accept or flag final redlines; procurement wants clarity on pricing tiers and committed capacity.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: and i want to confirm technical feasibility — KMS integration, vpc peering, and whether private deployment is necessary or hosted with tenancy/isolation will suffice.
[00:51] Sara Kim: and security — we need SOC2, encryption at rest and in transit, HSM/KMS support, and audit logs, plus deletion certificates for PHI.
[01:05] Jamie Cruz: understood. to start MSA/DPA — we sent the standard versions and highlighted the liabilities and data processing sections. any high-level reactions?
[01:20] Maya Singh: high level, liability cap in section 8 is lower than we'd like; we also want more explicit data residency statements and a deletion certification clause. some of the language around subcontractors is vague.
[01:32] Jamie Cruz: okay, fair. on liability cap we can propose escalation: for pilot/v1 we can keep standard, but for enterprise you can buy higher caps as a commercial amendment — is that acceptable?
[01:45] Tom Alvarez: procurement will need a written option table we can present to finance; also need to see penalty/remedy terms in the SLA to justify the premium.
[01:56] Priya Nair: for SLAs — we have a matrix: hosted API has 99.9% uptime with variable latency SLOs depending on plan; dedicated capacity adds stronger latency guarantees and a higher uptime commitment. i'll share the matrix after.
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: when you say latency SLOs, is that p95 or p99? what metrics do you expose?
[02:20] Priya Nair: primarily p95 for token-generation latency in hosted tiers, p99 available for dedicated/enterprise with tracing hooks. token-level and route-level breakdowns are available in the console.
[02:33] Sara Kim: and what happens on SLO miss — credits only or other remedies?
[02:37] Jamie Cruz: typically service credits; for enterprise deals we can discuss credits plus release clauses in extreme unavailable cases — but legal needs to weigh that.
[02:47] Maya Singh: we'll want explicit maximum remediation and a cap on credits; also need a failover policy if region goes down.
[02:54] Priya Nair: on routing — Redwood can route to alternative region or to dedicated pools as a fallback. we can document the automatic fallback policy.
[03:05] Tom Alvarez: pricing— procurement is focused on committed capacity for cost predictability. show us committed v. PAYG numbers and break-even points.
[03:15] Jamie Cruz: yes — we'll send a pricing scenarios spreadsheet (committed 6/12/24 month tiers) with example workloads. we'll also calculate token-unit cost after batch/caching optimizations.
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: for our workloads — mostly long-form summarization and some real-time chat. we need to know memory/KV-cache behavior for long contexts and whether quantized model variants are allowed for PHI data.
[03:40] Priya Nair: quantized variants are supported; for PHI we recommend private deployment or Dedicated with Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) so keys never leave your control.
[03:52] Sara Kim: BYOK is a hard requirement for us — plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:58] Jamie Cruz: we can support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations; we'll note the supported providers and steps in the security doc. audit logs export is supported via syslog/forwarding endpoints.
[04:10] Maya Singh: on DPA — we need deletion certs and sub-processor lists. does Redwood provide periodic attestation?
[04:18] Priya Nair: yes, we publish sub-processor list and can provide deletion attestation for customer data; for on-prem/private customers we can hand the keys to customer.
[04:27] Tom Alvarez: how long is data retained in hosted inference? default TTLs?
[04:31] Priya Nair: default session-level KV cache is ephemeral; logs/metrics retention depends on plan, but we have options for short retention windows and auto-delete on termination. we'll provide explicit retention matrix.
[04:44] Liam O'Connor: pilot timeline — we want a 4-week pilot with sample dataset in region A, then an extended 8-week test. what support does Redwood provide?
[04:54] Jamie Cruz: we provide a technical onboarding checklist, a dedicated SE for pilot, and 2 weeks of priority support included for pilots. if you need more SLOs or dedicated capacity we can scope that separately.
[05:06] Maya Singh: on the MSA redline, I flagged indemnity and data breach notification timelines — we usually require 48 hours notice. Redwood standard is 72; is 48 possible?
[05:18] Jamie Cruz: i can't commit on call, but historically we have some flexibility for enterprise deals. i'll capture that and discuss with contracts.
[05:26] Tom Alvarez: procurement also needs to know procurement routing and PO process — can you accept a net-60?
[05:33] Jamie Cruz: net-30 is standard, net-60 may be possible at enterprise tier with credit checks — we'll add that to the commercial scenarios.
[05:42] Sara Kim: for security artifacts, we need SOC2 report, ISO attestation if available, pen test summary, and architectural diagram for the hosted and private options.
[05:52] Priya Nair: we have a security pack — i'll share SOC2, pen test summary, and the infra diagrams. for private we'll include the on-prem package docs.
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: network-wise, do you support VPC peering or private link?
[06:06] Priya Nair: yes — VPC peering for dedicated and private deployments, and private link options for hosted API in supported regions.
[06:13] Maya Singh: one more legal point — termination rights on data. we want explicit deletion plus certificate within X days.
[06:20] Jamie Cruz: noted. we typically provide deletion cert within 14 days for hosted customers; we can confirm timing in the DPA redline.
[06:29] Tom Alvarez: will you be able to provide a redline by Thursday?
[06:31] Jamie Cruz: yes — i'll aim to send redlined MSA and DPA by 2026-06-18.
[06:36] Priya Nair: and i'll send the SLA/pricing matrix tomorrow with committed and PAYG comparisons.
[06:42] Maya Singh: great. a few questions from legal: do you have sub-processor flow-downs and can you add our required flow-downs for subcontractor liability?
[06:53] Jamie Cruz: we can add flow-downs for core data-processing sub-processors; for third-party infra providers we typically provide notice and a list. we'll discuss specifics offline.
[07:02] Sara Kim: on encryption at rest — can you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[07:07] Priya Nair: yes, BYOK is supported for enterprise hosted and for private. keys can be in AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or an HSM-backed solution; we'll share supported integrations.
[07:18] Liam O'Connor: any limitations for KV cache in private deployment?
[07:22] Priya Nair: private deployment gives you full control; we can tune KV eviction policies and cache lifetimes. for hosted we have safe defaults but configurable retention windows.
[07:33] Tom Alvarez: procurement question — what are the minimum commitment tiers for Dedicated?
[07:38] Jamie Cruz: min is typically 4 GPUs reserved for a 12-month term, but we can discuss smaller pilots on shorter commits; pricing will reflect that.
[07:49] Maya Singh: will you provide a separate SOW for onboarding work?
[07:52] Jamie Cruz: yes, SOW for onboarding and any engineering support is separate and we will include a statement of work template.
[07:59] Priya Nair: quick note on benchmarking — we'll share a spreadsheet template and we'd be happy to run a short benchmark on your sample prompts to show latency and cost tradeoffs.
[08:11] Liam O'Connor: that would be useful. also interested in model quantization effect on accuracy for our medical text.
[08:18] Priya Nair: we can provide comparison runs: 8-bit vs 4-bit quantized variants and regression metrics on your eval set — we'll need an NDA for datasets if they contain PHI.
[08:29] Maya Singh: NDA is in place? we have an existing vendor NDA but if Redwood needs a mutual NDA we can sign.
[08:36] Jamie Cruz: we have mutual NDA in our current paperwork — i'll confirm and attach.
[08:40] Tom Alvarez: on timeline — if we get redlines by Thursday and SLA/pricing tomorrow, procurement can aim for a finance review the following week.
[08:48] Jamie Cruz: sounds good. to recap next steps: redlined MSA/DPA by 6/18, SLA/pricing spreadsheet by tomorrow, security artifacts and SOC2/pen test, schedule security deep-dive w/c 6/22.
[08:59] Maya Singh: agreed. thanks everyone.
[09:02] Sara Kim: thanks.
[09:04] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[09:06] Jamie Cruz: appreciate your time — we'll follow up in email with attachments. bye.

End of transcript.
